owner_instruction: Fix the people side first, then port to the fantasy map.
problem: With the floodplain rule in production (calibration/floodplain_rule_20261114 A2), the whole-empire supply calibration fails narrowly (west->east transfer 89.2% < 90%). The heartland people pattern was rescaled to the committed field's window total, which puts 6.65 M people in Egypt proper (historical 4.5-5 M), so Egyptian farmers eat more of their own grain.
known_before_declaration: Egypt capacity with the rule 5.83 M; committed window total and the P2 totals inside the Roman 'allowed' mask have NOT been computed.

people_level_variants.frier: PRIMARY. Heartland pattern P2 = capacity (floodplain grid) x exp(-D/800) scaled so its total on the pool's Roman 'allowed' land equals 61.4 M (Frier 2000, Cambridge Ancient History XI, AD 164). The same factor applies off allowed land.
people_level_variants.absolute: P2 with no rescaling (capacity x occupancy as computed). Sensitivity.

production: Floodplain rule in supply production exactly as amendment A2 (scripts/floodplain_supply.py machinery), harvest grid output/land_people/earth_floodplain/earth.npz.
runs: For each level: whole empire and without Egypt.
rules: Original supply-calibration decision unchanged (270 km kept within ln 1.25 or 1.1 x best; transfer >= 0.90 both ways). Report Egypt-proper people against 4.5-5 M and e95 against the adopted 0.3923 (robust if within x1.25).
interpretation_declared: PASS on 'frier' whole empire = the Earth supply calibration passes with Egypt in development; its e95 is the Earth-supported share with Egypt. Then the floodplain rule is ported to the fantasy map as a separate declared step. A pass only on 'absolute' is reported but not used. A fail on both leaves Egypt open and the port still proceeds as the owner asked, with this result stated.
